Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significance of this period in your life and the importance of prioritizing your well-being as a new mother. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms. The purpose of this assessment is to understand your emotional experience during the postpartum period and to identify any potential concerns that may require additional support.

Please know that everything discussed in this session is confidential and respected. I'm here to provide a safe and supportive space for you to express your feelings and thoughts without judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional state over the past week. I'll ask these questions in a conversational manner, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you're comfortable.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. It's simply a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your postpartum experience. I'm here to listen, support, and provide guidance where needed.

Let's start with the first question. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself, in terms of being able to cope with things and manage your daily life as a new mother?

Honestly, it's been a bit of a struggle. I mean, I'm trying my best to take care of my baby and do everything I'm supposed to do, but some days I just feel so exhausted. The lack of sleep is really getting to me, and it's hard to keep up with all the new responsibilities. I feel like I'm managing, but just barely. There are times when I feel really overwhelmed and like I'm not doing anything right. I worry that I'm not doing enough for my baby or that I'm not being a good mother. But at the same time, I'm trying to remind myself that it's okay to not have all the answers and that I'm doing the best I can. It's just hard to shake off the feeling that I'm not coping as well as I should be. Some days are better than others, though. When I get a little more sleep or my baby has a good day, it feels like everything is going to be okay. But then there are days when everything feels like it's falling apart, and I just feel really tired and unsure of myself.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I'd say that's true for me, but not as much as it used to be. I mean, I still enjoy spending time with my baby and watching her little personality develop, and that brings me a lot of joy. But, to be honest, it's been a bit harder for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm so focused on making sure everything is okay with the baby and getting through each day that I don't have as much time or energy to laugh and have fun like I used to. Sometimes my husband will try to make me laugh, and it's nice, but it's just not as easy for me to find the funny side of things right now. I do still enjoy some things, like watching my baby smile or seeing her discover new things, but it's not like it used to be before she was born. I feel like I've lost a little bit of my sense of humor and my ability to not take things so seriously. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I used to love planning outings or trying new restaurants, but now it all just feels like so much work. Even simple things, like going for a walk or meeting a friend for coffee, feel overwhelming because I have to worry about the baby's schedule and whether she'll be fussy or not. And sometimes, by the time we get to the thing I was looking forward to, I'm just so exhausted that I don't even enjoy it anymore. 

I do look forward to some things, like my baby's bath time or reading her a bedtime story, but it's not the same as looking forward to things for myself. I feel like I've lost a bit of my own identity and sense of self, and that's hard for me. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going to a movie or trying a new hobby, but then I feel guilty because I think I should be spending that time with the baby instead. It's like I'm stuck in this cycle of just taking care of the baby and not really doing anything for myself, and that's hard to enjoy.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I'd say that's definitely been happening to me lately. As a new mom, I feel like I'm already questioning my abilities and wondering if I'm doing everything right, and when things don't go as planned, it's easy for me to blame myself. Like, if the baby is fussy or doesn't sleep well, I'll think to myself, "What did I do wrong? Is it because I didn't feed her enough or because I didn't burp her right?" And even if it's not really my fault, I'll still find a way to blame myself for it. 

It's hard for me to shake off the feeling that I'm not doing enough or that I'm not good enough. And sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me and tell me that everything is okay, but it's hard for me to believe him when I'm feeling so anxious and uncertain. I'll think to myself, "But what if I'm not doing this right? What if I'm messing up our baby's whole life?" It's like, I know it's irrational, but it's hard for me to stop those thoughts from creeping in. And it's not just about the baby, either - I'll also blame myself for things like not having a clean house or not cooking a good meal. It's like, I'm already feeling so overwhelmed and uncertain, and then I just pile on more guilt and self-blame, and it's hard to break out of that cycle.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something that might happen in the future. Like, I'll think to myself, "What if she gets sick? What if I'm not prepared for an emergency?" Or, I'll worry about things that are completely out of my control, like, "What if there's a power outage and we lose heat?" It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just can't seem to shake off these worries. 

And it's not just about big things, either. I'll worry about little things, like, "Is she eating enough?" or "Is she sleeping too much?" It's like, I'll be going about my day, and then suddenly I'll just start feeling this sense of unease or anxiety, and I won't even know what's causing it. My husband will try to reassure me, and he'll be like, "Everything is fine, the baby is healthy and happy," but it's hard for me to believe him when I'm feeling so anxious. 

Sometimes, I'll be up at night, feeding the baby, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios. It's like, I know I need to try to calm down and focus on the present moment, but it's hard for me to do that when I'm feeling so overwhelmed with worry. And it's not just about the baby, either - I'll worry about my relationship with my husband, or about how I'm doing as a mom, or about whether I'm losing myself in all of this. It's just... it's a lot, you know?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's like, I'll be thinking to myself, "What's wrong? What's happening?" And then I'll realize that there's no real reason for me to be feeling that way. The baby is fine, my husband is fine, everything is okay... but I still can't shake off that feeling of panic.

It's scary, because it feels like my body is just reacting to something, but I don't know what it is. And it's not just when I'm alone, either - sometimes it will happen when my husband is right there with me. He'll be like, "What's wrong? What's going on?" And I'll be like, "I don't know... I just feel really scared all of a sudden." It's hard to explain, because it doesn't make sense, even to me.

Sometimes, I'll try to distract myself by doing something else, like taking a deep breath or going for a walk, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic once it's started. And it's not just the feeling of panic itself - it's also the worry that I'll feel that way again, and that I won't be able to cope with it. It's like, I'm already feeling so overwhelmed and uncertain as a new mom, and then I have to deal with these random feelings of panic on top of it. It's just... it's a lot to handle, you know?

I think it's mostly been about the baby's health, to be honest. I'll worry that something is wrong with her, or that I'm not doing enough to keep her safe. And then that worry will just spiral out of control, and I'll feel like I'm going to panic. But, like I said, it's not always about something specific - sometimes it just feels like my body is reacting to some kind of invisible threat. Does that make sense?
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely been true for me lately. I feel like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a full-time job, and on top of that, I'm trying to manage the household, and cook meals, and do laundry... it's just exhausting. And it's not just the physical stuff, either - it's the emotional toll of being a new mom, too. I feel like I'm constantly worried about something, whether it's the baby's health, or my relationship with my husband, or just trying to figure out who I am as a mom.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeling like I'm doing okay, and then something will happen - the baby will cry, or my husband will need something, or I'll just feel overwhelmed - and it's like, everything will just come crashing down on me. I'll feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. It's like, I'm trying to be this perfect mom, and I'm trying to take care of everyone else, but I'm forgetting to take care of myself.

And it's not just the big things, either - it's the little things, too. Like, I'll be trying to make dinner, and the baby will be crying, and my husband will be trying to help, but I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. I'll be like, "I just can't do this right now." And then I'll feel guilty, because I know I should be able to handle it. I should be able to take care of my baby, and my husband, and myself... but sometimes, it just feels like too much.

I think that's one of the hardest things for me - feeling like I'm not in control, like things are just happening to me, and I'm not able to keep up. It's like, I'm trying to be this capable, competent person, but really, I'm just barely holding it together. And that's a hard thing to admit, because I feel like I should be stronger, I should be able to handle it all. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I need help.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been true for me, unfortunately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping lately, and I think it's because I've been feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed. Even when the baby is sleeping, I'll lie awake at night, worrying about everything and feeling like I'm just not doing anything right. It's like, my mind is racing, and I just can't seem to turn it off.

I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things I'm worried about, and it's just hard to calm down. And then, when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just really unsettling. Sometimes, I'll wake up feeling more anxious than when I went to bed, which is just exhausting.

It's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, either - it's the feeling of being tired all the time, and just not having the energy to do anything. I'll be sitting there, trying to feed the baby or change her diaper, and I'll just feel like I'm running on empty. It's like, I'm not even a person anymore - I'm just a zombie, going through the motions.

And it's hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, and to take care of myself, but it's just so hard to come by. I'll try to take naps during the day, but the baby will wake up, or my husband will need something, and it's just... it's just really tough. Sometimes, I'll feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and that's a really scary feeling.

I think, too, that the unhappiness and the sleeplessness are just kind of feeding into each other. I'll be unhappy, and then I won't be able to sleep, and then I'll be tired, and that will make me even more unhappy... it's just this vicious cycle, and I don't know how to break out of it.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I'd say that's true for me, unfortunately. There are times when I feel really down, and I don't know how to shake it off. It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about all the things I'm worried about, and all the things I'm not doing right, and it's just... it's hard to explain. It's like, I'm just feeling really overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it better.

Sometimes, it's just little things that will set me off. Like, the baby will cry, and I'll feel like I'm not doing enough to comfort her. Or, my husband will say something, and I'll take it the wrong way, and I'll just feel really hurt. And then, before I know it, I'm just feeling really sad, and I don't know how to stop it.

It's not all the time, though. There are times when I feel happy, and I'm enjoying being a mom, and everything feels okay. But the sad times... they're just really tough. And it's hard, because I feel like I should be happy all the time, now that I have this beautiful baby. But the truth is, being a mom is hard, and it's okay to not be okay.

I think, too, that I'm just feeling a little lost, you know? I used to be this person who had a job, and friends, and hobbies... and now, I'm just a mom. And that's a big adjustment, you know? It's like, I'm trying to figure out who I am, now that I have this new role. And it's hard, because I don't know if I'm doing it right. I don't know if I'm being a good mom, or if I'm just making it up as I go along.

So, yeah... I'd say I do feel sad or miserable, sometimes. But I'm trying to be kind to myself, and remind myself that it's okay to not be okay. And I'm hoping that, with time, things will get better, and I'll find my footing as a mom.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I'd say that's true for me, unfortunately. I've been crying a lot lately, and it's just really hard to stop once I start. It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeling overwhelmed, and then suddenly I'll just be crying. It's not always about something specific, either - sometimes it's just about everything. It's like, I'll be feeling really anxious, and then I'll just start crying, and I won't be able to stop.

Sometimes, it's just little things that will set me off. Like, the baby will cry, and I'll feel like I'm not doing enough to comfort her, and then I'll just start crying. Or, my husband will try to help me with something, and I'll just feel like he's not doing it right, and then I'll start crying. It's like, I'm just so sensitive right now, and everything just feels really overwhelming.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm crying all the time, and I don't know how to stop. I'll be sitting there, crying, and my husband will be like, "What's wrong? What's going on?" And I'll be like, "I don't know... I just feel really overwhelmed, I guess." And then he'll try to comfort me, and I'll just feel like I'm being a burden to him.

I think, too, that I'm just feeling really guilty about crying all the time. I feel like I should be stronger, and I should be able to handle everything without falling apart. But the truth is, being a mom is hard, and it's okay to not be okay. And I'm trying to remind myself of that, but it's just really hard right now.

I don't cry every day, though. It's just... sometimes. When I'm feeling really overwhelmed, or when things just feel like they're too much. And it's not always a lot of crying, either. Sometimes it's just a few tears, and then I'm okay. But other times... it's just really hard to stop.

* Persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and enjoyment in activities
* Difficulty sleeping, with sleep disturbances linked to mood and anxiety
* Overwhelming feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-blame
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed, particularly regarding the baby's health and well-being
* Crying spells and emotional reactivity to minor stressors

Consistent patterns across answers include:

* Low mood and loss of enjoyment in activities
* Difficulty coping with responsibilities and feeling overwhelmed
* Anxiety and worry about the baby's health, relationships, and personal identity

Potential areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression and anxiety include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt

This new mother presents with a constellation of symptoms and emotional concerns that suggest a potential risk for postpartum depression and anxiety. The patient's reports of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, combined with feelings of guilt and worthlessness, warrant further evaluation and monitoring. It is essential to continue assessing the patient's mental health and well-being, providing support and resources as needed to ensure their safety and the well-being of their baby.
